in the case of the synergic interaction of influenza viruses and chemical carcinogen in the pathogenesis and development of lung cancer, a complex of factors, including both viral and chemical carcinogens is necessary for the induction and the maintenance of the malignant transformation process in the lung.
the experimental data obtained so far do not permit the conclusion that viruses are the sole causative factors of lung cancer.

, on the basis of the results obtained so far, the problem of the joint action in the process of carcinogenesis of the influenza virus, and other viruses, and of chemical carcinogenic agents is not solved.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the results obtained in experimental studies are in favour of the synergic effect of the influenza virus (type A2 and A/PRS) and chemical carcinogens in lung cancer.
, in the light of our experimental studies and of the data of other authors, the synergic action in the pathogenesis in lung cancer of influenza viruses (A2, B) and of chemical factors, is a fact.
the influenza virus, in addition to its role of a respiratory pathogen, is also a carcinogen of the lungs.
The main takeaway from our work is that
influenza virus infection and chemical carcinogens may act synergistically in the pathogenesis lung cancer.
